analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/provider/cli-reference.md: it bumps the date, adds a drain-completion statement (head lines 443-447), and adds a handshake-deadline row at ~1943. No executable code or security controls changed.

New drain text: a graceful drain may complete without coordinator acknowledgement only when no work is left and the provider has no registered coordinator session (e.g. reconnecting); the CLI reports 'not needed (no coordinator connection)', and a registered session must still acknowledge before the deadline. This documents behavior of ProviderLoop+Lifecycle/ServiceDrain that is not in the supplied evidence. Relevant threats are T-053 (stale authorization) and T-010 (availability). The stated carve-out does not weaken the registered-session barrier. The usage-finalization and billing-safety implications of a drain with no coordinator session, and the exact condition used to decide 'no registered session', cannot be verified from this docs-only diff.

Handshake deadline row: a 30s deadline for TCP/TLS/WebSocket upgrade, with retry on reconnect backoff. This is a plausible availability hardening for TB-002. The implementation file CoordinatorConnectionHandshake.swift is not supplied, so the claim is unverified. No threat-model update is evident.

Unchanged surrounding docs cover logout/revocation (A-008), the SSD prefix cache (T-041) and Autopilot; none of it is altered by the diff. Remaining question for integration: whether the source changes behind these doc edits (drain without ack when unregistered; handshake timeout) exist in other batches and were reviewed there.
